title: Cut a release
summary: The release ritual: draft the changelog from merged PRs, tag the release behind an approval, publish notes, watch errors after rollout, and roll back if it goes sideways.

parts.title: Draft the changelog
parts.guidance: Compare the release candidate with the previous release tag and review the changes that actually remain in that range. Describe user-visible behavior and required upgrade actions, omitting reverted work and confidential issue details. Check migration instructions against the implementation. Keep links to the included changes and candidate revision so the notes can be corrected if the release contents change before publication.

execution.rationale: Compare Git revisions and draft release notes from the changes that remain in the candidate range.

parts.title: Tag the release
parts.guidance: Check the versioning convention, candidate commit and release checks, and confirm the proposed tag is unused. Inspect which workflows publishing it will trigger before using the release owner's authorization. Create the tag through the agreed release process and verify that the remote tag resolves to the reviewed commit. Follow any triggered build or publication so an unexpected side effect is caught at the release boundary.

execution.rationale: GitHub's reference API creates and reads the approved tag; workflow and check APIs inspect the triggered builds for that revision. Review release triggers before publishing the tag.

parts.title: Publish release notes
parts.guidance: Publish the cleared notes for the correct tag and audience through the authorized release channels. Confirm that described features are available to those users and that upgrade or migration links lead to the matching version. Check the public page after publication and give support that same reference, including any staged-rollout differences customers may see.

execution.rationale: GitHub's release API supports publishing the approved notes against the correct tag and checking the resulting page.

parts.title: Monitor errors post-release
parts.guidance: Compare the new release with the prior version over the rollout's observation window. Look for new error signatures, affected journeys and changes in impact, accounting for differences in traffic. Check support and on-call reports alongside telemetry. When a release criterion is breached, give the responder links to the relevant events and deployment, with enough context to distinguish a release regression from an unrelated incident.

execution.rationale: Sentry covers error events, but the required support and on-call correlation uses separate unidentified sources.

parts.title: Roll back if needed
parts.guidance: Identify the last working version and compare rollback with the incident's recovery needs. Check whether a database migration, running job or external side effect would remain after code is reverted. Carry out the release owner's chosen recovery action within its authorized scope, then repeat the affected user journey and data checks. Preserve the failure and recovery timeline for investigation, and update the service-status channel with the verified outcome.

execution.rationale: Recovery depends on the deployed platform, migrations and external effects; a generic code revert does not establish the mechanism.

links.when: Rollback criteria are met and the authorized release owner chooses rollback as the recovery action.

metadata.supportReason: Changelogs, tags, and release notes are pure API work. Deciding to roll back is a human call.
